transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door hinge / balance / springs (drops open). Check the dishwasher's plug is fully in and its socket or the switched spur (often a switch above the worktop) is on, and try another appliance in that socket. If the electrics have tripped, don't keep resetting it. Was a switch, plug or fuse off (and is it sorted), or does the socket work fine with something else?
The dishwasher has power and washes fine, so it's not an electrics problem. It's just the door that drops open. I heard a twang noise last week when it went.
Open the door, check nothing in the racks or the cutlery basket sticks out, then shut it firmly until it clicks and press start. Does it still show the door as open?
It doesn't show the door as open, the door closes and latches fine and it washes ok. The problem is just that it drops open with no resistance when I open it.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
The checks point to the door hinge. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on the side edge of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The sticker on the door edge is partly peeled, so I can only read the start, it says LTF. I can't see the rest of it.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
Next: On an integrated machine check the furniture-door alignment/balance. Let me know what you find.

The door closes square and the hinges look straight from what I can see. The decor panel is the same one that was fitted originally. When I open the door the left side still has some tension but the right side has none.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
This is a mechanical failure and cannot be fixed by adjustment. Because this requires dismantling the door to access the internal springs/cables, it is best handled by an engineer. They will need to replace the faulty right-side hinge/balance unit (and often recommend checking the left side too since they wear together). You can still use the dishwasher safely; just support the door with your hand when opening and closing it until a repair is made. When you have a moment, try to get the full model number from that sticker so we can confirm exactly which hinge kit fits.
